question: When a more reactive metal is placed in the salt solution of a less reactive metal, it:
solution:
The correct answer is __**displaces the less reactive metal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **displacement reaction** is a type of chemical reaction where a **more reactive metal** displaces a **less reactive metal** from its **salt solution**. This occurs because the more reactive metal has a greater tendency to lose electrons and form positive ions.
 
• The relative reactivity of metals is determined by the **Reactivity Series** (or activity series), which is an arrangement of metals in **descending order** of their chemical activities. Metals at the top of the series, such as **Potassium** and **Sodium**, are highly reactive, while those at the bottom, like **Gold** and **Platinum**, are the least reactive.
 
• During this process, the more reactive metal undergoes **oxidation** as it loses electrons to become an ion in the solution. Conversely, the less reactive metal ion in the salt solution undergoes **reduction** as it gains those electrons to form a neutral metal atom.
 
• A classic example is the reaction between **Iron (Fe)** and **Copper sulfate (CuSO4)** solution. Since **Iron** is more reactive than **Copper**, it displaces the copper from its solution, resulting in the formation of **Ferrous sulfate (FeSO4)** and **Copper (Cu)** metal. ***Hence, the correct answer is that it displaces the less reactive metal.***
 
• If a **less reactive metal** is placed in the salt solution of a **more reactive metal**, no chemical change occurs. For instance, if **Copper** is placed in a **Zinc sulfate** solution, there is **no reaction** because copper is lower than zinc in the reactivity series.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Reactivity Series:**
 
 
• The standard order of reactivity (from most to least reactive) is **Potassium (K)**, **Sodium (Na)**, **Lithium (Li)**, **Calcium (Ca)**, **Magnesium (Mg)**, **Aluminium (Al)**, **Zinc (Zn)**, **Iron (Fe)**, **Tin (Sn)**, **Lead (Pb)**, **Hydrogen (H)**, **Copper (Cu)**, **Mercury (Hg)**, **Silver (Ag)**, and **Gold (Au)**.
 
• **Hydrogen**, although a non-metal, is included in the series because it also forms positive ions and serves as a reference point for comparing the reactivity of metals with **acids** and **water**.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Applications:**
 
 
• **Thermite Reaction:** A displacement reaction where **Aluminium** powder reacts with **Iron(III) oxide** to produce molten iron. This reaction releases a massive amount of heat and is used for welding **railway tracks** and broken machine parts.
 
• **Metal Extraction:** Highly reactive metals like **Sodium** or **Aluminium** are used as **reducing agents** to displace metals like **Chromium** or **Manganese** from their respective oxides during the smelting process.
 
• **Galvanization:** To protect iron from **corrosion**, it is coated with **Zinc**. Because zinc is more reactive, it reacts with environmental oxygen and moisture first (sacrificial protection), effectively displacing the oxidation process away from the iron.
 
 
 
• **Observation of Reactions:**
 
 
• Displacement reactions are often accompanied by a **color change** in the solution. For example, when **Iron** nails are placed in **blue-colored Copper sulfate**, the solution gradually turns **light green** due to the formation of **Iron sulfate**.
 
• Visible deposits also form; in the **Iron-Copper** reaction, a **reddish-brown** layer of copper metal is deposited on the iron nail.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Redox Nature:** Every single displacement reaction is a **Redox reaction**, meaning **Reduction** and **Oxidation** happen simultaneously. The metal that is more reactive is **oxidized**, and the metal ion that is displaced is **reduced**.
 
• **Reaction with Water and Acids:** Metals at the very top (K, Na) react **violently** with **cold water** to produce **Hydrogen gas**, while metals like **Magnesium** react only with **hot water**. Metals below **Hydrogen** in the series do not displace hydrogen from **dilute acids**.
 
• **Chemical Equations:** A general representation is **A + BC → AC + B**, where **A** is more reactive than **B**. If **B** were more reactive than **A**, the reaction would be represented as **A + BC → No Reaction**.
